summary: Craig County, Virginia, tower on Potts Mountain in Jefferson National Forest; a June 1936 item has a fire warden on its steel tower; listed as gone.

facts.design: Steel fire tower (per a June 1936 item quoted by Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no removal date in the sources read.

events.note: June 1936 Danville Bee item, quoted by Forest Lookouts: a bear raiding sheep in the Potts Creek section held a fire warden on his steel fire tower until after supper

evidence.supports: Location: Craig County (Forest Lookouts page heading)
Agency: Jefferson National Forest (Forest Lookouts page heading)
Date of the Danville Bee item: June 1936
Fire warden on his steel fire tower; bear kept him there past suppertime
evidence.quote: the bear kept him on his steel fire tower past supper time

evidence.supports: Bear's depredations on sheep were in the Potts Creek section
evidence.quote: depredations on sheep in the Potts creek section

evidence.supports: Fire warden suggested immediate action by telephone
evidence.quote: He suggested immediate action by telephone

evidence.supports: Two men with rifles killed the bear (275 pounds)
evidence.quote: The 275-pound bear fell to the rifles of Marshall Taylor and Murrel Helms

evidence.supports: Association list: Potts Mountain, Craig County, tower, status Gone
Neighboring Bald Mountain was one of two Craig County towers built in 1955
evidence.quote: One of two towers built in Craig County in 1955

evidence.supports: Potts Mountain was the other mountain in the county with a tower
evidence.quote: Bald Mountain runs parallel to Potts Mountain, the other mountain that was home to a tower in this county.

evidence.supports: Hiker's own search: nearly everything found refers to the more northern Craig County site, which is not on the Appalachian Trail
evidence.quote: Nearly everything I have found refers to the more northern lookout site in Craig County that is not on the Appalachian Trail.

evidence.supports: The Appalachian Trail site is labelled Stony Creek and is in Giles County
evidence.quote: says Stony Creek Lookout Tower on the map and is located in Giles County

evidence.supports: The Stony Creek site is near the Appalachian Trail
evidence.quote: The lookout location that the Appalachian Trail passes near

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the 1936 staffing detail rests on one Forest Lookouts page quoting the Danville Bee; the newspaper itself was not read. No build year, height, owner or removal date appears in any source read. The Bald Mountain register entry does not date the Potts Mountain tower, so the story does not assign it a build year. The hiker's page covers a Giles County site near the Appalachian Trail (labelled Stony Creek) that is a different site; it is cited only as a warning, not as part of this record. The Association point (37.54191, -80.21801) has no second source to check it. Next check: Jefferson National Forest or Craig County history for a build year and removal date.
